title: PM core (package manager internals)
tldr: PM has three separate generation stores (app venv, PM runtime, side environments) with their own selection file, lock, lease and collector; side environments are never collected (PMC-01).

Biggest kill: the hand-mirrored worker IPC (pm/client.py wrappers, pm/worker_operations.py string table, per-op branches in pm/worker.py) plus package-definition marshalling with no production consumer (PMC-02, PMC-08).
Biggest simplification: one frozen Install layout value replaces pm/paths.py, six manifest.json probes and the worker's runtime monkeypatch of pm.paths (PMC-03).
Low-hanging (high severity, effort S/M): 4 — PMC-02, PMC-03, PMC-04, PMC-06.
pm/ is several overlapping mechanisms around a good core (pinned store + one uv engine); its API is wide: 42 facade names plus 176 imports into 25 submodules.

modules.owns: built-in package catalog (19 Package subclasses incl. Venv)
tool-store installs, app-venv sync, PATH activation, drift
hermes pm subcommands; re-exec into the PM runtime
resumable ranged downloader (also LLM model files)
install layout, selected venv, boot activation, shell exports
upstream index scrapers for pm update
content store of published entries, fetch, extract, digests
PythonEnvironment: the single uv argv builder
caller-side proxy to the per-call worker
plugin discovery to uv workspace; npm sidecar
PM's own isolated interpreter: prepare, lease, collect, launch
PM install lock, publication journal, leases, app-generation GC

findings.title: Three generation stores (app venv, PM runtime, side environments) implement the same select-last protocol three ways; side environments are never collected
findings.problem: The app venv (<installs>/<key>/environments/<uuid>, selected by the venv fact in per-install facts.json), PM's runtime (pm-runtime/generations/<uuid>, selected.json, .prepare.lock) and side environments ($HERMES_HOME/environments/<name>/gen-<hex>, active.json, .install.lock) each implement build-fresh, flush, write-record-last, keep-previous, lease, collect. Three record shapes, three identity hashes, two collectors with different age rules, and no collector for side environments (rg finds only the validator at pm/operations.py:141), so every requirement change leaves a whole venv behind. GC is invoked from two copies (pm/cli.py:518-523, hermes_cli/venv_sync.py:139-145). Durability and Windows-hold fixes must land three times.
findings.move: Add pm/generations.py::Generations(root) with build(identity, builder) -> Path, selected(), lease(), collect(min_age) and one frozen Selection record (generation, identity, meta). App venv, PM runtime and side environments become three Generations roots. Lease/GC code from hermes_cli/runtime_state.py moves in. The venv fact in per-install facts.json becomes the app root's selection record.

reference.pattern: frozen value class for the Selection record

findings.risk: Boot activation reads the selection before imports (pm/environments.py:380-438): the record must stay stdlib-readable and the lock/lease ordering in activate_dependencies must hold. Old installs keep the venv selection in facts.json: one release of read-compat.

findings.title: The worker IPC boundary is hand-mirrored in three files, with a second direct code path per operation that diverges
findings.problem: Each operation exists as an implementation (pm/install.py, pm/operations.py, pm/build_operations.py), a client wrapper restating its full signature with hand Path->str conversion (11 near-identical wrappers, client.py:273-421), and a string row in worker_operations.py resolved by getattr(import_module). worker.py special-cases operations by name (102-111). Errors cross a hard-coded 7-type map (client.py:74-76). Eight `if is_runtime(): direct(...)` sites give every operation a second path; the paths diverge: client.sync_venv's foreign-interpreter guard (client.py:209-220) is absent on the direct path and pm/cli.py::_install_python_environments calls pm.install.sync_venv directly. One parameter change touches three files and two transports.
findings.move: One @operation(needs=..., bootstrap=...) decorator on implementations records function objects in a registry; one generic proxy pm._remote.call(fn, **kwargs) serializes from inspect.signature (one codec for Path and plugin inputs); the worker calls registry[name](**kwargs) with no per-op branches; InstallError family gets to_wire/from_wire. Delete pm/client.py wrappers and pm/worker_operations.py; the facade exports the decorated functions.

reference.pattern: one typed message envelope (msg_header/msg/serialize) for every message type

findings.risk: Worker must keep running on the PM runtime's stdlib + 4 deps; facade must stay lazy (PEP 562) so pm.environments boot stays cheap. Tests monkeypatching pm.client.X break.

findings.title: Install layout is rediscovered per call by free functions split over two modules, and the worker monkeypatches pm.paths at runtime
findings.problem: Source checkout, sealed payload (manifest.json), Nix/Docker resident runtime (install-stamp.json) and borrowed HERMES_HOME are re-derived on every call by functions in pm/paths.py that delegate back into pm/environments.py. Six sites probe manifest.json with two different anchors. HERMES_RUNTIME_DIR and HERMES_INSTALL_ROOT override pieces. The worker injects its context by assigning lambdas over pm.paths.repo_root and lockfile_path (worker.py:72-73), a process-global rebinding. Owner/borrower resolution (environments.py:41-91) drew 3 fixes in the latest week of history.
findings.move: A frozen Install value (kind: source|payload|resident; repo, lockfile, store, writable_store, state_dir, tool_facts, selection) built once by Install.discover(project_root), passed explicitly to Store/Generations/operations and carried in the worker request. Delete pm/paths.py; pm/environments.py keeps only boot activation.

reference.pattern: frozen value + evolve for derived layouts

findings.risk: pm.environments must stay importable with stdlib + hermes_constants at boot. 15 hermes_cli imports of pm.paths move to Install. Resolve HERMES_HOME at call time (profile-scope rule).

findings.title: PM and hermes_cli import each other; PM's own lock, lease and publication journal live in hermes_cli/runtime_state.py
findings.problem: PM claims independence from the application graph (pm/runtime.py:1-5; Dockerfile:202-207 copies only pm/ + hermes_constants.py), yet the worker imports hermes_cli.config (lazy policy), hermes_cli.runtime_state (its own install lock/journal/leases), private hermes_cli.auth._file_lock and hermes_cli._launchers._launcher_python, hermes_cli.update_receipt, urllib_security, plugins_manifest, macos_signing, root utils, scripts.bundles.native, and tools/agent modules for package verification. Import matrix: pm->hermes_cli 26 lazy edges; hermes_cli->pm 24 eager + 144 lazy. hermes_cli/runtime_state.py imports only pm + stdlib: it is PM code filed under the app. Each pm-only bootstrap stage breaks on whichever path first reaches one of these imports, and only on that install kind.
findings.move: Move the body of hermes_cli/runtime_state.py into pm/ (pm/generations.py, PMC-01) and keep a forwarder at the old path (tests/compat/old_updater_surface.json pins the file). Lazy policy arrives as request data (PMC-07). _file_lock and _launcher_python move into pm or are passed in; package verify hooks needing agent/tools take a caller-supplied callable. Add an import-linter contract: pm imports only stdlib, its 4 runtime deps, hermes_constants, hermes_platform.

reference.pattern: install manager imports only util.package; config passed in via pip_kwargs()

findings.risk: Old updaters import hermes_cli.runtime_state mid-swap; the forwarder must re-export every current name. Tests patch hermes_cli.runtime_state._atomic_bytes.

findings.title: The package manager parses and writes every profile's config.yaml plugin selection and replaces plugin trees, duplicating the plugin loader's enablement rules
findings.problem: PM re-parses config.yaml with its own validator and enablement rules (plugins_state.py:22-79), separately from hermes_cli/plugins_discovery.py:112-122; writes plugins.enabled/disabled and memory.provider via ruamel round-trip (publication.py:76-101, plugin_eviction.py:90-125); swaps plugin directories and .install-metadata.json (publication.py:142-175); and recovers from a journal whose two row shapes are handled in hermes_cli/runtime_state.py:62-136. Four mutually exclusive PluginInput kinds select the behaviour. The memory-provider rule is encoded twice. Two definitions of 'enabled' can disagree.
findings.move: Keep the atomic guarantee, make it generic: PM sync takes members: list[Path] and an optional Publication(files: dict[Path, bytes], trees: list[(target, staged)]) of opaque bytes prepared by the plugin layer; PM journals and commits them with the selection and never parses YAML. Enablement reading and eviction policy move to hermes_cli/plugins_*. PluginInput collapses to members + publication; pm/plugins_state.py and the YAML editing in publication.py/plugin_eviction.py leave pm/.

reference.pattern: loader asks the requirements manager for installs only; it never writes config entries

findings.risk: Commit must stay atomic across config bytes, plugin tree and selection; recover_publication must still run before activation (pm/environments.py:394-396). Shared with seams 11-plugins and 03-pm-flows.

findings.title: The app venv is forced into the Package hierarchy as a StatePackage; one Facts class stores two record types across two files with a legacy fallback
findings.problem: Venv subclasses Package yet uses none of url/fetch/unpack/stage/verify/env, and overrides expected_stamp with a different signature. Four isinstance(StatePackage) branches and a 'state' bootstrap tier paper over it; pm.ensure('venv') silently becomes sync_venv. Facts mixes tool records (entry/version/env/artifacts/digest) and the venv record (stamp/extras/environment/resolved_lock), told apart by 'entry' in fact. The venv record is read with a fallback to the store facts file at 4 sites. pm/install.py (983 lines) holds both engines.
findings.move: Venv stops being a Package: delete StatePackage, the isinstance branches and the 'state' tier. Split pm/install.py into pm/tools.py (store installs, PATH) and pm/appenv.py (venv sync). Two frozen records, ToolFact and EnvSelection (= PMC-01 Selection). Drop the store-file venv fallback after one migration.

reference.pattern: define(frozen=True) typed records instead of shape-sniffed dicts

findings.risk: Sealed payload facts.json files keep the old shape and must still read. hermes_cli/doctor_platform.py:420 imports pm.packages.Venv.

findings.title: Install consent is decided in 19 places from an explicit bool, a repair flag, a bootstrap tier, an env var used as IPC, and a config read inside the PM worker
findings.problem: rg 'lazy_installs_allowed\(\)|_refuse_lazy\(' pm finds 19 decision sites; `explicit` appears 128 times across pm/. The worker reads security.allow_lazy_installs through hermes_cli.config (install.py:179-190) and the client forwards policy by setting HERMES_DISABLE_LAZY_INSTALLS=1 in the child env (client.py:67). No single place says which operations may download.
findings.move: One Consent value (explicit | lazy_allowed | lazy_refused | repair) decided once at the entry point (CLI, or the ensure_import caller in the app process) and carried in the request. The worker never reads config or env for policy; Operation.bootstrap folds into the same check.

reference.pattern: skip_pip policy applied in one place, pip_kwargs computed once

findings.risk: Docker and the hermetic test harness set HERMES_DISABLE_LAZY_INSTALLS; it stays an entry-point input.

findings.title: Package-definition marshalling across the worker seam has no production consumer
findings.problem: Every worker request serializes module/qualname/file/namespace paths for non-pm.packages Package classes and the worker re-imports them with a spec_from_file_location fallback and synthetic namespace modules (~90 lines). No production code registers a Package outside pm/packages.py and pm/security_packages.py (only tests and an unregistered scripts/termux/stage_runtime_libs.py:54 subclass). pm.security_packages is already a built-in module (registry.py:17) yet is marshalled on every request. The facade exports register/Package publicly. Root AGENTS.md rejects extension points without a consumer.
findings.move: Delete package_definitions, load_package_definitions, the request 'packages' field and the worker call; stop exporting register from the facade. If plugin-defined packages are ever needed, discover them by entry point inside the worker.

reference.pattern: entry-point discovery instead of shipping class identities over IPC

findings.risk: tests/pm/test_worker_registry.py and tests/pm/test_runtime_bootstrap_tls.py:140 fixtures go; they test only this mechanism.

findings.title: Two urllib client configurations with divergent redirect/TLS policy, per-site timeouts, nested retries, and upstream scrapers split from their packages
findings.problem: Opener A (downloader, https-only redirects, stdlib TLS) and opener B (hermes_cli.urllib_security, follows https->http with header stripping, truststore) differ; store.hash_url imports the downloader's private _OPENER/_UA. Timeouts are literals (60/120/600/60/60). Ranged fetch downgrades inside retry_network inside a per-mirror loop; sources are probed twice. Three Windows-hold retry loops use three schedules. Single-consumer scrapers (node, martin-riedl, btbn, pbs, llama) live in update.py apart from Package.latest_versions; GitHub pagination is copied 3 times. Download also serves dashboard model downloads with no sha256.
findings.move: One stdlib pm/http.py client object (one opener, https-only redirects, truststore, one UA, a Timeout value, one retry policy with jitter) used by the downloader, hash_url and scrapers; one replace_with_retry helper; move single-consumer scrapers onto their Package classes; one GitHub pagination helper. Keep the range/resume core.

reference.pattern: one long-lived client with a typed Timeout (httpx/_config.py:72); retries as in stamina/_core.py:119

findings.risk: Mirror fallback, pause semantics and Windows AV holds must be preserved. pm must stay stdlib-only: copy the shape, not the dependency.

findings.title: Eleven build/CI operations ship in the runtime facade and route through the per-call worker; four different ways reach the PM runtime
findings.problem: build_environment, lock_project, stage_manager_runtime, ensure_environment, ensure_project_environment, check_project_lock, export_requirements, build_requirements_environment, prepare_tools, stage_tools and prune_cache have no in-scope runtime caller (rg per name: callers are scripts/, CI, Dockerfile, pm/build_env.py, pm/cli.py). The PM runtime is reached by CLI re-exec (run_cli, parsing argv twice), per-call worker, direct is_runtime() calls, and the always-direct stage_manager_runtime.
findings.move: One rule: PM code runs inside the PM runtime. CLIs (pm.cli, pm.build_env) re-exec once via run_cli; only the app-facing runtime API (ensure, sync_venv, venv_is_current, ensure_python_tool, ensure_import) uses the worker. Build ops move to pm/build/ and leave the facade and worker table.

reference.pattern: install is one in-process call owned by the CLI

findings.risk: scripts/ callers switch from pm.build_environment etc. to pm.build.

findings.title: Receipts are ambient ContextVar state with copy-on-write and cross-process correlation glue
findings.problem: Four ContextVars, deep-copy-on-write records, a correlation id read from hermes_cli.update_receipt, a worker context and a client-side accept_worker_receipt re-filing step; record_* calls scattered across install.py, client.py, plugin_eviction.py; a 35-line docstring explaining the hazards. The plugin update cadence also writes into PM receipts (record_plugin_checks).
findings.move: sync_venv creates a Receipt object, passes it explicitly to the helpers that record, and returns it (the worker already returns it). The updater attaches the returned receipt to its own. record_plugin_checks moves to the plugin cadence's receipt.

reference.pattern: explicit manager instance state (install_failure_history) instead of ambient globals

findings.risk: The updater embeds sync sections by correlation id; that contract becomes a return value.

findings.title: No narrow public API: 176 imports reach 25 pm submodules; TID251 bans name modules that do not exist and are bypassed by a re-export
findings.problem: Beside the 42-name facade, consumers import 25 submodules directly (scripts/pmc_consumers.py). TID251 bans pm.uv, pm.client.uv, pm.install.uv (none exist) plus pm._uv, pm.environment, pm.runtime_stage; the pm.environment ban is bypassed by pm/workspace.py:33 re-exporting ResolutionConflict, consumed at hermes_cli/plugins_admission.py:76. Private names cross module lines (_is_member_candidate, _refuse_lazy, downloader._OPENER, update._get_json).
findings.move: Public surface = facade (runtime API) + pm.environments (boot). Replace the six TID251 entries with one import-linter forbidden contract: outside pm/, import only pm and pm.environments. Delete the workspace.py:33 re-export.

reference.pattern: single public package over private implementation modules

seam_answer: pm/ is not one package manager with one model. It has a good core: a pinned, hash-verified tool store (Lockfile, Store, Facts, Download) and a single clean uv engine (PythonEnvironment). Around it sit four layers that each re-implement an idea: three generation stores (PMC-01), a hand-mirrored IPC layer with two code paths per operation (PMC-02, PMC-10), a plugin-config transaction system that belongs to the plugin layer (PMC-05), and a path model rediscovered per call and patched at runtime (PMC-03). The API is wide: 42 facade names plus 176 imports into 25 submodules; 'environment' names four modules, 'operations' three, plugin logic five. A simonw/hynek-quality version: one Install value, one Store of pinned tools, one Generations primitive for app venv/PM runtime/side environments, one @operation registry behind one transport, a six-name runtime facade (ensure, ensure_import, sync_venv, venv_is_current, ensure_python_tool, env_for), pm.environments for boot, pm.build for CI; plugin config edits arrive as opaque bytes committed with a selection. Deletable: definition marshalling, client wrappers and routing table, pm/paths.py, StatePackage, the legacy facts fallback, stale bans; about -1,300 lines in pm/ before tests.

cross_seam.note: PM's boot/update half lives in hermes_cli (venv_sync 626, _early_recovery 684, boot_bootstrap 247, update_completion 313); generation GC duplicated with pm/cli.py:518-523
PM re-implements plugins.enabled/disabled semantics and the memory.provider union separately from the plugin loader
PM writes user config.yaml via ruamel round-trip outside the config system
hermes pm bypasses argparse registration by sniffing sys.argv[1:2] == ['pm']
worker Popen, run_cli and the Windows PowerShell native-build spawn have no overall timeout
any marker-evaluation failure reads as 'supported'; any config error reads as 'lazy installs refused'
package definitions import tools/agent modules for env and provenance checks
dashboard model downloads use pm.downloader.Download without a sha256
